[ota-hal] OTA-1761 — the one that was not broken

Owner, on the corrected screenshot: *"those 2 images have the misalignment
again, the one before it was fine."* It was. This reverts OTA-1760's change to
FirstTimeHint's tips link and leaves the file exactly as it shipped.

1. ⚠⚠⚠ BOTH HALVES OF MY DIAGNOSIS WERE WRONG, AND THAT IS THE PASS
   OTA-1760 measured the link's label sitting at the left edge of its own
   padding box and called it an off-centre tap target:
       Got it         box x284.2 w72.3 · text x303.2 w34.3 → 19.0 / 19.0
       Turn off tips  box x 54.5 w71.4 · text x 54.5 w61.4 →  0.0 / 10.0
   · THE BOX IN THE SCREENSHOT WAS THE HEADLESS BROWSER'S FOCUS RING. On a
     device that control has no border at all, so nothing was visibly
     off-centre. ⚠ OTA-1760's own commit message SAYS the ring is an artifact
     and warns against acting on it — and then acts on it. Naming an artifact is
     not the same as not being fooled by it.
   · THE TAP TARGET WAS NEVER ASYMMETRIC. `hitSlop={8}` on that
     TouchableOpacity already extends the touchable area 8pt on ALL FOUR sides.
     "No tap forgiveness at all to the left of the label" was asserted without
     reading the JSX it was about — the line sits four lines from the style I
     changed, in a block I had already read in this same session.

2. ⚠⚠ THE SHIPPED VALUES WERE RIGHT ON BOTH THINGS A PLAYER CAN SEE
       label x 54.5 — FLUSH with the card's body text above it
       box   x 54.5 — 18.0 from the card's inner edge, matching `Got it`'s
                      18.0 on the other side
   Both fall out of `paddingLeft` being absent and the card's padding being 18.
   There is no third value that satisfies both, which is why each attempt broke
   the half the other preserved:
       marginLeft: -10    label stayed flush · box fell to 8.0 from the card
       offset deleted     box back to 18.0   · label indented 10pt from the body
   The owner caught each one from the render, and was right each time. The
   second report came with both screenshots side by side, pointing at each
   failure mode in turn.

3. WHAT THIS DOES NOT REVERT
   ⚠ OTA-1760's VendorScreen half stays. That was a real defect — the
   placeholder's line box ended at y=122 and the back button's began at y=122,
   so a 1px border sliced the sentence above it — and the same button was
   stretched to the full column with no header row to sit in. Both fixed, both
   measured, both untouched here. A revert of one half is not a reason to lose
   the other, and a test in the new suite asserts that it survived.

4. THE RECORD, NOT JUST THE REVERT
   `linkBtn`'s comment now says DO NOT centre it again, and why: the focus ring
   is still in every harness shot and it will still look off-centre to the next
   reader. A silent revert would invite the same "fix" a third time. The suite
   asserts the note is present, asserts `hitSlop` is on the same control the
   claim was about, and pins the shipped padding byte for byte.
   ⚠ `__tests__/ota1760…` keeps a comment where its second block used to be,
   rather than dropping it: that pass shipped two changes and only one survived,
   and a suite that quietly lost the other would read as though it had always
   been about VendorScreen alone.

⚠⚠ THE LESSON, STATED SO IT OUTLIVES THIS COMMIT: the harness is a MEASUREMENT
tool, and a measurement of the wrong thing is still a number. Everything I
measured here was accurate — the boxes really are 0.0/10.0 — and the conclusion
was still wrong, because the box being measured is not drawn on a device and the
property being fixed was already provided by a prop I did not read. Two passes
of confident, numerically-supported work on a defect that did not exist. The
owner's amendment says actual-device appearance is the final visual acceptance
authority; this is what it looks like when the harness is treated as more than
that.

Tests: __tests__/ota1761TheOneThatWasNotBroken.test.tsx (7 tests) — the shipped
padding pinned byte for byte with the two attempted values asserted absent;
⚠ `hitSlop={8}` proved to sit on the SAME control the asymmetry claim was about,
which is the fact that made the whole diagnosis wrong; the card's 18 proved to be
where both the label's flush alignment and the box's inset come from, so a later
reader can see why no third value exists; the link proved still quiet, still
underlined, still borderless; the DO-NOT note proved present in the file where
the next reader will be rather than only in this message; and OTA-1760's Vendor
fix proved to have survived the revert.
